name: Push-up
tips: Hands shoulder-width apart, body in a straight line from head to heels
Lower chest to floor with elbows at 45° from body — not flared wide
Don't let hips sag or pike — squeeze glutes throughout

name: Squat
tips: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward
Break at hips and knees together — keep chest tall and upright
Drive through heels on the way up, knees tracking over toes

name: Bent-over Row
tips: Hinge at hips to ~45°, back flat, core braced before you pull
Pull elbows back and up, squeezing shoulder blades at the top
Don't jerk or use momentum — control both the pull and the return

name: Plank
tips: Forearms or hands below shoulders, body in a perfectly straight line
Squeeze glutes and brace core as if bracing for a punch
Don't let hips sag or rise — breathe steadily and hold

name: Lunge
tips: Step forward keeping your torso upright — don't lean
Front knee tracks over ankle, back knee lowers close to the floor
Push through your front heel to return — don't let knee cave inward

name: Deadlift
tips: Bar over mid-foot, grip just outside legs, back flat before lifting
Think 'push the floor away' not 'pull the bar up'
Drive hips forward at the top — don't hyperextend your lower back

name: Bench Press
tips: Slight arch in upper back, shoulder blades squeezed and tucked
Lower the bar to your lower chest — touch lightly, don't bounce
Drive feet into floor for leg drive and press in a slight arc

name: Pull-up
tips: Start from a dead hang with arms fully extended
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving elbows down and back
Avoid kipping — control the descent for maximum muscle development

name: Shoulder Press
tips: Brace core tight — don't arch your lower back as you press
Lower dumbbells to chin/upper chest height, elbows slightly forward
Press straight up, not forward — think tall, vertical movement

name: Bicep Curl
tips: Pin elbows to your sides and keep them there throughout
Squeeze hard at the top, then lower slowly — take 3 seconds down
Don't swing your body — eliminate momentum for better gains

name: Tricep Dip
tips: Lean slightly forward to target triceps — upright hits chest more
Lower until elbows reach 90°, then drive through palms to press up
Keep shoulders down — don't let them shrug up toward your ears

name: Russian Twist
tips: Lean back to ~45°, feet raised or on floor for easier variation
Rotate from your torso — not just swinging your arms side to side
Slow and controlled gets better results than fast and sloppy

name: Incline Push-up
tips: Same form as a regular push-up — hands elevated on a bench or step
Lower the surface height to make it progressively harder over time
Keep body in a straight line from head to heels throughout

name: Chest Fly
tips: Keep a slight bend in elbows throughout — never fully lock out
Lower until you feel a good stretch in your chest — don't overstretch
Squeeze chest to bring dumbbells back up, leading with elbows

name: Lat Pulldown
tips: Lean back slightly, chest up — pull bar to your upper chest
Lead with elbows driving down and back, not your hands
Never pull behind your neck — it puts harmful strain on your spine

name: Seated Row
tips: Sit tall with core braced — pull the handle to your belly button
Squeeze your shoulder blades together fully at the end of the pull
Control the return slowly — don't let the weight snap back

name: Superman
tips: Lie face down, arms extended forward, forehead lightly on floor
Lift arms, chest and legs simultaneously — hold 2 seconds at top
Focus on a slow, controlled lift — not a jerk or snap

name: Glute Bridge
tips: Feet flat on floor hip-width apart, knees bent at 90°
Drive hips up by squeezing glutes hard — hold 1–2 seconds at top
Don't hyperextend your lower back — tuck pelvis slightly at the top

name: Calf Raise
tips: Use a step for full range of motion — heel drops below platform level
Pause at the bottom for a stretch, pause at top for peak contraction
Go slow — calves respond well to time under tension

name: Step-up
tips: Drive through the heel of the elevated foot — not the back foot
Keep your torso upright — don't lean forward excessively
Control the descent slowly — don't just drop back down

name: Wall Sit
tips: Back flat against wall, thighs parallel to floor, knees at 90°
Weight through heels — toes can lift slightly if needed
Breathe steadily and hold — arms on thighs or extended forward

name: Mountain Climber
tips: Start in a strong plank position — hips level, core tight
Drive knees toward chest alternately — keep hips from rising
Faster = more cardio burn, slower = deeper core engagement

name: Bicycle Crunch
tips: Rotate from your shoulders — not just twisting your neck
Fully extend the straight leg low to the floor as you twist
Slow and controlled every rep beats fast and sloppy every time

name: Leg Raise
tips: Press your lower back firmly into the floor before you start
Keep legs straight or slightly bent — lower slowly with control
Stop just before feet touch the floor to keep tension on the core

name: Side Plank
tips: Stack feet or stagger them for better stability as a beginner
Hips up — body in a straight line from head to feet
Don't let your hip drop toward the floor — keep it elevated

name: Lateral Raise
tips: Slight bend in elbows — raise arms to shoulder height only
Lead with your elbows, not your hands or wrists
Keep shoulders down — don't shrug. Use lighter weight with control

name: Arnold Press
tips: Start with palms facing you at chin height, elbows close together
Rotate palms outward as you press up — full rotation by the top
Reverse the rotation on the way down — slow is better

name: Hammer Curl
tips: Palms face each other (neutral grip) throughout the entire movement
Elbows stay pinned to your sides — isolate the bicep and brachialis
Great for building forearm and upper arm thickness

name: Burpee
tips: Jump or step feet back to a solid plank — chest to floor is optional
Explosive jump at the top — clap hands overhead for a full rep
Scale by removing the jump or the push-up to suit your level

name: Kettlebell Swing
tips: Hip hinge, not a squat — the power comes from snapping your hips forward
Drive hips explosively to swing the bell to shoulder height
Arms just guide the bell — your glutes and hips do all the work
